standard_prerequisites.name: The general characterization of strictness
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the equivalence between strictness of a morphism and the canonical map from its coimage to its image being an isomorphism.

standard_prerequisites.name: Short exact sequences and associated graded objects
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the exactness of the sequences of graded pieces is equivalent to the graded pieces of coimage and image being isomorphic, which gives the equivalence of (3) with (4), (5) and (6).

standard_prerequisites.name: The five lemma
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the five lemma for abelian categories
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the conclusion of the descending induction from the commutative diagram whose rows are short exact sequences.

core_obligations: (1) and (2) (proof lines 5262-5263): their equivalence is the cited general characterization of strictness.

(3), (4), (5) and (6) (proof lines 5264-5267): the cited lemma on short exact sequences and graded objects shows that the exactness of the three displayed sequences is equivalent to the graded pieces of the coimage and of the image being isomorphic.

(3) implies (2) (proof lines 5268-5290): it suffices to show that an injective and surjective map of finite filtered objects inducing an isomorphism on the associated graded induces an isomorphism of filtered objects, that is that it maps each filtration step onto the corresponding step; this is proved by descending induction on the index, the induction step being the commutative diagram with short exact rows whose outer vertical maps are known and whose middle map is then an isomorphism by the five lemma.
proof_roadmap: Reduce strictness to the canonical map from coimage to image being an isomorphism.
Translate that into exactness of the sequences of graded pieces by the companion lemma.
Reduce the remaining implication to a map that is injective and surjective and induces an isomorphism on the graded pieces, and finish by descending induction with the five lemma.
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects six equivalent conditions on a morphism of finite filtered objects: strictness, the canonical map from coimage to image being an isomorphism, the same after applying the associated graded functor, exactness of the two short sequences of graded pieces and of the four-term sequence of graded pieces (statement lines 5234-5259). The proof is a complete argument: the first equivalence is the general characterization of strictness, and the equivalence with the three exactness conditions is attributed to a named lemma on short exact sequences and graded objects (proof lines 5262-5267); the remaining implication is reduced to showing that a map which is injective, surjective and an isomorphism on the associated graded maps each filtration step onto the corresponding one, which is done by descending induction using a commutative diagram with short exact rows and the five lemma (proof lines 5268-5290). The non-formal content is the descending induction. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
